question: Does cost-charged gradient-alignment selection still beat random selection when random training on the candidate pool helps the target, i.e. when candidates come from the target's own domain? And does it beat not training at all?
motivation: In stage 69 random training on news/English candidates raised the Arabic Wikipedia target loss, so alignment's advantage was mainly avoidance of harm. Stage 70 draws Arabic candidates from Arabic Wikipedia itself and pre-specifies the no-update baseline.
hardware: One Colab GPU, NVIDIA L4 (as assigned in stage 69) or A100. The device is journaled with the calibration; a resumed session on a different device type aborts, so all runs of a model use one device type.
models: Qwen2.5-0.5B and Qwen2.5-1.5B, revisions and weight SHA-256 exactly as in research/llm-gpu-scale-protocol.json.
numerics_and_adapters: As stage 69: float32, TF32 off, deterministic algorithms, CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:4096:8; LoRA rank 8, alpha 16 on q_proj and v_proj; AdamW lr 5e-4, weight decay 0; one 65-token chunk per update.
data: Arabic Wikipedia, wikimedia/wikipedia revision b04c8d1ceb2f5cd4588862100d08de323dccfbaa, file 20231101.ar/train-00004-of-00007.parquet (SHA-256 f035e9118745d465529d48b0b1893824a4f266af2474694dcd35823e767aad17). Eligible articles: at least 65 tokens. Excluded: the stage-69 probe and target articles. From the remaining eligible articles: probe = first 65 tokens of 16 articles (seed 7001); target = first 65 tokens of 256 different articles (seed 7002); Arabic candidates = first 65 tokens of every other remaining eligible article. Off-target candidates: UD-EWT English train chunks (r2.15, Qwen tokenizer). Each candidate slot is English with probability rho.
no_update_baseline: The target loss of the freshly initialised adapter (B = 0, so identical to the base model), recorded at step 0 of every run.
policies: Identical to stage 69 for the three arms.
schedule: Per model, rho index k and seed: rng = default_rng(seed + 1000 k); 4096-by-4 language flags, Arabic-candidate indices, English indices, then 4096 choices in [0,4).
budget: Per model, before any target evaluation: calibration seed 35999, rho 0.5, 24 steps per arm on candidates only; cost = median of steps 5-24 with CUDA synchronisation. Budget = 400 random-step costs; N_arm = floor(400 c_random / c_arm + 1e-9).
primary: Qwen2.5-1.5B, rho 0 (in-domain candidates): graddot4_batched at its N minus random at 400, mean over six seeds, with paired seed-bootstrap 95% interval (seed 7003, 10000 resamples). Negative favours graddot4_batched.
secondary: Same contrast for 0.5B and for rho 0.9; loss4 minus random; each arm minus the no-update baseline (pre-specified here, unlike stage 69); selection and throughput terms; English share. Intervals for secondary contrasts are descriptive; no multiplicity adjustment; no pooling across models.
prediction: Stated before running: at rho 0 random training should lower target loss (in-domain), so the throughput term should favour random and the outcome is open. At rho 0.9 the stage-68/69 pattern (alignment wins) is expected.
resumption: Journal (JSON lines) on Google Drive; completed (model, rho, seed, arm) entries are skipped; schedule digests and the evaluation sample are re-verified on resume.
coverage: 2 models x 2 rho x 6 seeds x 3 arms = 72 runs plus two calibrations.
audit: CPU audit as stage 69: journal digest, summary recomputation, budgets, evaluation and candidate samples, schedules, random choices and English shares.
scope: One model family, LoRA, short budgets, one GPU type, Arabic Wikipedia (possibly present in Qwen pretraining).
